tasks.title: Sec A · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the man from the conversation?

options.A: He has distinguished himself in foreign service.
options.B: He is his country’s ambassador to Winopia.
options.C: He is currently an electrical engineer.
options.D: He craves attention from the media.

questions.cn: 从这段对话中，我们能了解到关于男士的什么？

optionsCn.A: 他在外交工作中表现卓越。
optionsCn.B: 他是本国驻维诺皮亚的大使。
optionsCn.C: 他目前是一名电气工程师。

questions.stem: What does the man say the government of Winopia is probably undergoing?

options.B: A fundamental reform.
options.C: Some sort of political reorientation.
options.D: Some sort of crisis of legitimacy.

questions.cn: 男士说维诺皮亚政府可能正在经历什么？

optionsCn.A: 政府改组。

questions.stem: According to the man, how does one get a career in foreign relations?

options.A: All diplomats have more or less similar stories to tell.
options.B: It is a prerequisite to get some practice in diplomacy.
options.C: Different people can take different paths.
options.D: It is a must to first obtain a law degree.

questions.cn: 根据男士，一个人如何从事外交关系这一行？

optionsCn.A: 所有外交官的经历都大同小异。
optionsCn.B: 先积累一些外交实践经验是前提。
optionsCn.C: 不同的人可以走不同的路。

questions.stem: What do the speakers mainly discuss by the end of the conversation?

options.A: Key skills required of a diplomat.
options.B: The making of an expert diplomat.
options.C: Diplomatic discourse and rhetoric.
options.D: Contributions by diplomatic envoys.

questions.cn: 对话结束时，两位说话人主要在讨论什么？

optionsCn.A: 外交官所需的关键技能。

lines.t: Today’s special guest is Lord Blackwell, one of our country’s most experienced and distinguished career diplomats.
lines.cn: 今天的特邀嘉宾是布莱克韦尔勋爵，我国最有经验、最杰出的职业外交官之一。

lines.t: It’s my pleasure.
lines.cn: 这是我的荣幸。

lines.t: Our audience will be most interested in learning about a career in the foreign service.
lines.cn: 我们的听众会非常有兴趣了解外交部门的职业生涯。

lines.t: However, before we talk about that, I’d like to ask you about the current developments hitting the news today regarding the Republic of Winopia.
lines.cn: 不过，在谈这个话题之前，我想先请您谈谈今天新闻里关于维诺皮亚共和国的时事进展。

lines.t: What can you tell us?
lines.cn: 您能跟我们说些什么？

lines.t: I’m afraid I don’t know much beyond what we’ve all seen on the news.
lines.cn: 恐怕除了大家在新闻里看到的，我知道的并不多。

lines.t: It looks like the government of Winopia seems to be undergoing some sort of crisis of legitimacy and an interim administration has been transitionally established until a head of state is agreed on.
lines.cn: 看起来维诺皮亚政府似乎正经历某种合法性危机，在确定国家元首之前，已过渡性地成立了一个临时政府。

lines.t: But my career work has mostly focused around the Continental spheres of Europe and the Americas, and thus I’ve never been involved with Winopian relations.
lines.cn: 但我职业生涯的工作主要围绕欧洲大陆和美洲地区，因此我从未参与过与维诺皮亚的关系事务。

lines.t: It’s for this reason that I don’t know anything on this matter beyond what we can all read in the newspapers.
lines.cn: 正因如此，除了大家在报纸上能读到的内容，我对这件事一无所知。

lines.t: Oh, I see.
lines.cn: 哦，我明白了。

lines.t: Nevertheless, be rest assured that our export envoys at our consulate there will be closely monitoring the situation and I expect our bilateral relations with that country will not be affected.
lines.cn: 尽管如此，请放心，我们驻当地领事馆的商务外交人员会密切关注局势，我认为我们与该国的双边关系不会受到影响。

lines.t: So how does one get a career in foreign relations?
lines.cn: 那么，一个人怎样才能从事外交关系这一行呢？

lines.t: There are many different paths one can take.
lines.cn: 可以走的路径有很多。

lines.t: All diplomats have their own story.
lines.cn: 每位外交官都有自己的故事。

lines.t: But in my case, I got a degree in electrical engineering followed by six years’ service in the Air Force.
lines.cn: 就我而言，我先拿了电气工程学位，之后在空军服役六年。

lines.t: Then I went to a law school and upon obtaining a degree in international law, I joined the diplomatic core where I’ve been for 22 years.
lines.cn: 然后我去读了法学院，取得国际法学位后加入了外交队伍，至今已有 22 年。

lines.t: What would you say are the key skills one needs for the job?
lines.cn: 您认为这份工作最需要的关键技能是什么？

lines.t: There are so many.
lines.cn: 要具备的太多了。

lines.t: Being a hard worker and good student is important--you never stop learning.
lines.cn: 做一名勤奋的工作者和好学生很重要——你永远不能停止学习。

lines.t: In addition, a diplomat needs to be very articulate in their discourse and rhetoric.
lines.cn: 此外，外交官在言谈和辞令上必须非常清晰有力。

lines.t: Whether it is diffusing tension or enacting policy, people and communication skills are vital.
lines.cn: 无论是缓和紧张局势还是推行政策，人际交往和沟通能力都至关重要。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: Why does the man suggest they call it a day?

options.A: They have got their work done.
options.B: They both look tired.
options.C: They can meet again tomorrow anyway.
options.D: They are both anxious to go home.

questions.cn: 男士为什么提议今天就到这儿？

optionsCn.A: 他们已经把工作做完了。
optionsCn.C: 反正他们明天还能再碰。

questions.stem: What does the woman say is a little tough?

options.B: Two months devoted to the same contract.
options.C: Working two months without any progress.
options.D: The man’s long concentration on the project.

questions.cn: 女士说什么有点难熬？

optionsCn.A: 董事会成员支持不足。
optionsCn.B: 两个月都扑在同一份合同上。
optionsCn.D: 男士长期专注于这个项目。

questions.stem: What does the man say the woman must be in thinking they’ll finish by next week?

options.B: Inspirational.
options.C: Exceptional.
options.D: Delusional.

questions.cn: 男士说女士认为下周就能完工，一定是处于什么状态？

optionsCn.A: 不专业。

questions.stem: What does the entire managerial hierarchy want to see according to the woman?

options.B: More support from the board members.
options.C: The early implementation of the project.
options.D: The alignment of all sections of the contract.

questions.cn: 根据女士，整个管理层都希望看到什么？

optionsCn.A: 合同少一些整改。

lines.t: It’s getting late and we’re both displaying signs of weariness.
lines.cn: 时间不早了，我们俩都显出疲态了。

lines.t: I think we should call it a day and meet again tomorrow morning.
lines.cn: 我看今天就到这儿吧，明天早上再碰。

lines.t: Oh, come on Jeff.
lines.cn: 哦，别这样，杰夫。

lines.t: We are so close.
lines.cn: 我们就差一点了。

lines.t: Don’t you think we’re almost done?
lines.cn: 你不觉得我们快做完了吗？

lines.t: Let’s do two more hours, please.
lines.cn: 再干两个小时吧，求你了。

lines.t: One hour, then I’m going home.
lines.cn: 一个小时，然后我就回家。

lines.t: OK, fine.
lines.cn: 好，行。

lines.t: I think we are making good progress and that with a few more amendments we will be all done.
lines.cn: 我觉得我们进展不错，再改几处就全部完成了。

lines.t: I’m sure looking forward to it.
lines.cn: 我真是盼着那一天。

lines.t: I’m so tired of this project.
lines.cn: 这个项目让我太累了。

lines.t: Don’t get me wrong--it’s a great professional opportunity for me and a milestone for the company, but it’s just been so long.
lines.cn: 别误会——这对我来说是个很好的职业机会，对公司也是里程碑，只是拖得太久了。

lines.t: Yeah, two months working on nothing but the same contract is a little tough.
lines.cn: 是啊，两个月只做同一份合同，确实有点难熬。

lines.t: Nevertheless, I think that with a bit of luck we’ll be done by next week.
lines.cn: 不过，我想运气好的话，下周我们就能完工。

lines.t: Ha!
lines.cn: 哈！

lines.t: You must be delusional.
lines.cn: 你肯定是在做梦。

lines.t: You don’t think so?
lines.cn: 你不这么认为？

lines.t: No chance.
lines.cn: 绝无可能。

lines.t: Sections four, five, eight and nine still have to be aligned in the new framework.
lines.cn: 第四、五、八、九节还得按新框架对齐。

lines.t: Then we need to proofread the whole thing and make sure all selling points are watertight.
lines.cn: 然后我们得通篇校对，确保所有卖点都滴水不漏。

lines.t: But that will all take no more than a couple of days.
lines.cn: 但那也就花个两三天。

lines.t: I wasn’t finished.
lines.cn: 我还没说完。

lines.t: When we are done with it and send it upstairs, what do you think will happen?
lines.cn: 等我们做完交上去，你觉得会发生什么？

lines.t: What?
lines.cn: 什么？

lines.t: They’ll argue about it for like a month.
lines.cn: 他们会为此争论一个月。

lines.t: There’s always going to be the odd board member who intervenes and demands rectifications be made.
lines.cn: 总会有一两个董事插进来，要求做出整改。

lines.t: They might think they’re being helpful but in reality they’re being obstructive and hampering progress.
lines.cn: 他们可能自认为是在帮忙，但实际上是在阻挠、拖慢进度。

lines.t: Oh Jeff, you’re too preoccupied and cynical.
lines.cn: 哦，杰夫，你想得太多，也太愤世嫉俗了。

lines.t: It won’t be anywhere as bad as that.
lines.cn: 根本不会那么糟。

lines.t: You’ll see.
lines.cn: 你等着看吧。

lines.t: The entire managerial hierarchy wants to see this project implemented as soon as possible and the board too is virtually unanimous in its support.
lines.cn: 整个管理层都希望这个项目尽快落地，董事会也几乎一致支持。

lines.t: Go on then, let’s stop there and meet up again, same time tomorrow.
lines.cn: 那就这样吧，我们到这儿，明天同一时间再碰。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 3 组
tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: When can it be hard to know whom to believe?

options.A: When two employees propose contrary solutions to their dispute.
options.B: When two employees are directed by their respective manager.
options.C: When two people behave in an apparently clashing manner.
options.D: When two people tell different stories of the same event.

questions.cn: 什么时候会难以判断该相信谁？

optionsCn.A: 当两名员工对纠纷提出相反方案时。
optionsCn.B: 当两名员工分别受各自经理指挥时。
optionsCn.C: 当两个人行为明显冲突时。
optionsCn.D: 当两个人对同一件事说法不同时。

questions.stem: What does the speaker definitely recall about the dispute mentioned as an example?

options.B: How it happened.
options.C: What it was about.
options.D: When it was settled.

questions.cn: 关于举例提到的那场争论，讲话者清楚记得什么？

optionsCn.A: 它是如何解决的。

questions.stem: What did the speaker and his counterpart do when the two employees gave different accounts of the same event?

options.A: They intervened promptly lest their dispute escalate.
options.B: They tried to ascertain the actual facts of the matter.
options.C: They assumed the best about them and moved on.
options.D: They persuaded them to put their conflict aside.

questions.cn: 当两名员工对同一件事给出不同说法时，讲话者和他的同级经理做了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们及时介入，以免争论升级。
optionsCn.B: 他们试图查明事情的真实经过。
optionsCn.C: 他们做了最好的假设，然后向前看。
optionsCn.D: 他们说服两人把冲突放到一边。

lines.t: One thing I’ve learned in a quarter century of management is that there are ample gray areas in human behavior and that there may not always be clear right-or-wrong solutions to employee disputes.
lines.cn: 二十五年管理生涯教给我的一件事是：人的行为中有大量灰色地带，员工纠纷未必总有非黑即白的解决方案。

lines.t: When two people have different versions of the same event, it can be hard to know whom to believe.
lines.cn: 当两个人对同一件事有不同说法时，很难判断该信谁。

lines.t: One such circumstance always comes back to me.
lines.cn: 有这样一种情形，总是浮现在我脑海里。

lines.t: It happened years ago and it’s a measure of the forgettable nature of the conflict that I no longer even recall what the dispute was about, but I definitely recall the resolution.
lines.cn: 那是多年前的事了，这场冲突之不起眼，以至于我连争论的内容都不记得了，但我清楚记得它的解决方式。

lines.t: Two talented young executives, one of whom I was managing, had vastly different accounts of the same event and it seemed likely we’d never get to the truth.
lines.cn: 两位才华出众的年轻主管——其中一位由我管理——对同一件事的描述大相径庭，看起来我们永远查不出真相。

lines.t: We reached the deadlock.
lines.cn: 我们陷入了僵局。

lines.t: And the manager of the other individual said, “Here’s something I learned from an excellent manager I once worked for.”
lines.cn: 另一位主管的经理说：“这是我曾为之工作的一位出色经理教给我的。”

lines.t: He used to say, “when in doubt, assume positive intent.”
lines.cn: 他过去常说：“拿不准的时候，就假定对方出于善意。”

lines.t: And just like that, we had a path forward.
lines.cn: 就这样，我们有了前进的方向。

lines.t: My counterpart and I agreed we might never ascertain the actual facts of the matter.
lines.cn: 我和对方经理都同意，我们可能永远无法查明事情的真实经过。

lines.t: Quite likely there were elements of truth in both employees’ stories.
lines.cn: 很可能两位员工的讲述里都各有几分实情。

lines.t: We agreed to monitor their actions and relationship going forward, but to intervene no further.
lines.cn: 我们商定今后继续观察他们的行为和关系，但不再进一步介入。

lines.t: We assumed the best about both of them and moved on.
lines.cn: 我们对两人都做了最好的假设，然后继续往前走。

lines.t: The result was that we were able to put the conflict behind us.
lines.cn: 结果是，我们得以把这场冲突抛在身后。

lines.t: In fact, their problems didn’t recur.
lines.cn: 事实上，他们的问题没有再出现。

lines.t: Over the years this general approach has proved useful.
lines.cn: 多年来，这一通用做法被证明很有用。

lines.t: Whenever the truth is obscure, assuming positive intent and agreeing to move on can be a constructive decision.
lines.cn: 当真相不明时，假定善意并同意向前看，可以是一个建设性的决定。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 4 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do an increasing number of Americans do according to the passage?

options.B: Budget sensibly.
options.C: Enjoy cooking.
options.D: Shop at groceries.

questions.cn: 根据文章，越来越多的美国人在做什么？

optionsCn.A: 每天外出就餐。

questions.stem: What does Eddie Yoon think cooking is akin to?

options.B: Sewing.
options.C: Entertaining oneself.
options.D: Fashion designing.

questions.cn: 埃迪·尹认为做饭和什么相似？

optionsCn.A: 购物。

questions.stem: What will Americans be able to do by making their own lunch?

options.B: Cut down expenses.
options.C: Eat more healthily.
options.D: Cultivate new hobbies.

questions.cn: 自己做午餐能让美国人做到什么？

optionsCn.A: 满足自己的口味。

questions.stem: What does the passage say signifies a host of challenges for America’s grocery industry?

options.B: People’s deteriorating family finances.
options.C: People’s strong aversion to junk foods.
options.D: People’s increasing dislike of cooking.

questions.cn: 文章说，什么对美国的食品杂货行业意味着一系列挑战？

optionsCn.A: 人们对便利的高度追求。
optionsCn.B: 人们日益恶化的家庭财务状况。
optionsCn.C: 人们对垃圾食品的强烈反感。
optionsCn.D: 人们对做饭越来越不喜欢。

lines.t: For some Americans, going out to dinner is a treat, planned and budgeted for.
lines.cn: 对一些美国人来说，外出吃饭是一种犒赏，要计划、要预算。

lines.t: For others, it’s just a daily occurrence.
lines.cn: 对另一些人来说，这不过是日常。

lines.t: And that second group of people is becoming the majority, as the number of Americans who enjoy cooking is declining.
lines.cn: 而第二类人正在成为多数，因为享受做饭的美国人数量在下降。

lines.t: In the early 2000s, researcher Eddie Yoon conducted a survey to ascertain Americans’ attitudes to cooking.
lines.cn: 本世纪初，研究者埃迪·尹做了一项调查，以了解美国人对做饭的态度。

lines.t: The survey found that 15% of Americans loved to cook, 50% said they hated to cook and 35% reported mixed feelings.
lines.cn: 调查发现，15% 的美国人热爱做饭，50% 的人说讨厌做饭，35% 的人感受复杂。

lines.t: When Yoon conducted the same survey 15 years later, only 10% of respondents reported a love of cooking, 45% said they hated it, and 45% had mixed feelings.
lines.cn: 15 年后尹再做同一项调查时，只有 10% 的受访者表示热爱做饭，45% 说讨厌，45% 感受复杂。

lines.t: Yoon asserts cooking is akin to sewing.
lines.cn: 尹断言，做饭和缝纫很相似。

lines.t: As recently as the early 20th century, many Americans sewed their own clothing.
lines.cn: 就在 20 世纪初，许多美国人还自己缝制衣服。

lines.t: Today, the vast majority of Americans buy clothing; only a tiny minority still sew and they do it mainly as a hobby.
lines.cn: 如今，绝大多数美国人买衣服；只有极少数人还在缝纫，而且主要是当作爱好。

lines.t: Yoon believes the number of home cooks will diminish in a similar fashion.
lines.cn: 尹认为，在家做饭的人数也会以类似方式减少。

lines.t: Currently, the average American household spends over $3,000 per year on dining out.
lines.cn: 目前，美国家庭平均每年在外出就餐上花费超过 3000 美元。

lines.t: However, what people save in convenience, they lose in cash.
lines.cn: 然而，人们在便利上省下的，正是金钱上失去的。

lines.t: Take buying lunch on work days, for example.
lines.cn: 以工作日买午餐为例。

lines.t: People spend on average $10 per meal when they buy lunch.
lines.cn: 人们买午餐时平均每餐花 10 美元。

lines.t: Making your own lunch, meanwhile, will cost less.
lines.cn: 而自己做午餐则花费更少。

lines.t: One survey found people only spend on average $6.30 when they bring lunch prepared at home.
lines.cn: 一项调查发现，人们带家里做好的午餐时，平均只花 6.30 美元。

lines.t: Americans’ growing aversion to spending time in the kitchen signifies a host of challenges for the grocery industry.
lines.cn: 美国人对下厨越来越反感，这对食品杂货行业意味着一系列挑战。

lines.t: It’s likely to detrimentally impact family finances as well.
lines.cn: 它还可能对家庭财务状况造成不利影响。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 5 组
tasks.context: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What is the number one reason a bag ends up lost according to this talk?

options.A: Its owner’s flight is delayed because of bad weather.
options.B: Airlines cannot find its owner without an ID tag on it.
options.C: Airline staff have not correctly coded its destination tag.
options.D: Its owner has forgot to pick it up from the baggage claim.

questions.cn: 根据这段讲话，行李最终丢失的第一大原因是什么？

optionsCn.A: 行李主人的航班因恶劣天气延误。
optionsCn.B: 行李上没有身份标签，航空公司找不到主人。
optionsCn.C: 航空公司员工没有正确编码其目的地标签。
optionsCn.D: 行李主人忘了去行李提取处取走。

questions.stem: What may happen to your baggage even when there are sophisticated automated systems?

options.A: Its tag may get torn off on the conveyor belt.
options.B: Its tag may get stuck in the sorting machine.
options.C: It may be sent to a wrong destination.
options.D: It may be picked up by someone else.

questions.cn: 即使有先进的自动化系统，你的行李仍可能发生什么？

optionsCn.A: 它的标签可能在传送带上被扯掉。
optionsCn.B: 它的标签可能卡在分拣机里。
optionsCn.C: 它可能被送往错误的目的地。

questions.stem: What does the speaker advise us to do at the end of the talk?

options.A: Purchase irretrievably lost things at auction.
options.B: Contact the airport staff to find our missing bag.
options.C: Get the airline agent’s phone number before boarding.
options.D: Avoid packing valuable items in our checked baggage.

questions.cn: 讲话者在最后建议我们怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 在拍卖会上购买彻底遗失的物品。
optionsCn.B: 联系机场工作人员寻找丢失的行李。
optionsCn.C: 登机前拿到航空公司工作人员的电话号码。
optionsCn.D: 避免在托运行李中放贵重物品。

lines.t: Every year, of the more than 2.5 billion bags checked onto flights worldwide, 26 million go missing.
lines.cn: 每年，全世界有超过 25 亿件行李托运，其中 2600 万件丢失。

lines.t: And of that 26 million, 1 million never make it back to their original owner.
lines.cn: 而在这 2600 万件中，有 100 万件再也没能回到原主人手中。

lines.t: Bad weather and flight delays, miscoded destination tags, and some people simply forgetting to pick up one of their bags are a few of the reasons.
lines.cn: 恶劣天气和航班延误、目的地标签编码错误，以及有些人干脆忘了取走一件行李，都是部分原因。

lines.t: But the number one reason a bag ends up lost is that it has no ID tag and airlines don’t know to whom it belongs.
lines.cn: 但行李最终丢失的第一大原因是：它没有身份标签，航空公司不知道它属于谁。

lines.t: Transferring baggage from check-in to departure gates to arrival gates to baggage claim is a delicate piece of timing.
lines.cn: 把行李从值机柜台运到登机口、再到到达口、再到行李提取处，是一件时间拿捏很精细的事。

lines.t: If the system moves too slowly, the bags won’t make connecting flights.
lines.cn: 如果系统运转太慢，行李赶不上转机航班。

lines.t: If it’s too fast, the bags may make the connection, but the passengers might miss the flight.
lines.cn: 如果太快，行李也许赶上了转机，但乘客可能误了航班。

lines.t: Each airport has its own way of allotting how much time a bag needs to move in transit.
lines.cn: 每家机场都有自己的方式来分配行李中转所需的时间。

lines.t: Some airports have sophisticated automated systems, including scanners that read baggage labels, destination coded vehicles that load and unload the bags without stopping, and sorting machines that route baggage to the appropriate gate.
lines.cn: 一些机场配有先进的自动化系统，包括读取行李标签的扫描仪、不停机装卸行李的目的地编码小车，以及把行李分拣到相应登机口的分拣机。

lines.t: Even so, all that technology may not save your baggage tag from being torn off on the conveyor belt, making you the owner of a bag with no name.
lines.cn: 即便如此，这些技术也未必能保住你的行李标签不在传送带上被扯掉，让你成为一件无名行李的主人。

lines.t: Once a bag goes missing and the passenger files a claim, the bag is declared mishandled by the carrier.
lines.cn: 一旦行李丢失、乘客提出索赔，这件行李就会被承运方认定为“处理不当”。

lines.t: Mishandled refers to bags that have been delayed, lost, stolen or damaged.
lines.cn: “处理不当”指行李被延误、丢失、被盗或损坏。

lines.t: Most delayed bags are only one flight behind their owners and can be delivered within 24 hours.
lines.cn: 大多数被延误的行李只是比主人晚一个航班，可在 24 小时内送达。

lines.t: The other bags are examined by airline employees for clues to their ownership and destination.
lines.cn: 其余行李则由航空公司员工检查，寻找关于其归属和目的地的线索。

lines.t: If the mystery is solved, those bags are returned to their owners within four or five days.
lines.cn: 如果谜团解开，这些行李会在四五天内归还主人。

lines.t: Bags with no destination code or identification tag are shipped to a central warehouse and undergo a comprehensive baggage tracing process over the next 90 days.
lines.cn: 没有目的地代码或身份标签的行李会被运往中央仓库，在随后 90 天内经历全面的行李追踪流程。

lines.t: Airlines inventory their mishandled baggage, and many use a database to match the contents with owners’ descriptions.
lines.cn: 航空公司会对处理不当的行李登记造册，许多公司用数据库把行李内容与主人的描述进行匹配。

lines.t: It takes about three months to go from missing in action to irretrievably lost.
lines.cn: 从“下落不明”到“彻底遗失”，大约需要三个月。

lines.t: Once that happens, the bags are donated to charity, sold at auction, or purchased by a company which sells them to the public.
lines.cn: 一旦到了这一步，这些行李会被捐给慈善机构、在拍卖会上出售，或者被一家公司收购后转售给公众。

lines.t: So never pack anything of real value in your checked baggage and make sure your name is on the bag along with your phone number so an agent can contact you.
lines.cn: 所以，千万不要在托运行李里放任何真正贵重的东西，并确保行李上有你的姓名和电话号码，以便工作人员联系你。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 6 组
tasks.context: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about using one smartphone during a face-to-face conversation?

options.B: It can be especially disappointing.
options.C: It can be socially harmful.
options.D: It can be really embarrassing.

questions.cn: 关于面对面对话中使用手机，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它在行为上可能有危险。

questions.stem: How did the participants in the new study respond regarding phone use during social interactions?

options.B: They held a negative view towards it.
options.C: They were concerned with its effects.
options.D: They saw it as a sign of social evolution.

questions.cn: 新研究中的参与者对社交互动中使用手机持什么态度？

optionsCn.A: 他们认为这不可避免。
optionsCn.D: 他们把它看作社会进化的标志。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say can result from the common behavior of using phones during face-to-face conversations?

options.B: Ill effects on one’s sense of pride.
options.C: Poor relationships with others.
options.D: Vicious cycles of detachment.

questions.cn: 讲话者说，面对面对话中使用手机这一常见行为可能导致什么？

optionsCn.A: 复杂精细的社交接触形式。
optionsCn.B: 对个人自尊的不良影响。

lines.t: You’ve probably been with someone who ignored you while interacting with his or her smartphone, and you’ve probably engaged in this behavior yourself.
lines.cn: 你大概遇到过这样的人：跟你在一起时只顾玩手机、不理你——而你自己大概也做过这种事。

lines.t: In a recent survey, nine out of ten respondents said they’d used their smartphone during their most recent social activity.
lines.cn: 在最近一项调查中，十分之九的受访者说，他们在最近一次社交活动中用过手机。

lines.t: There’s also evidence that this behavior is socially harmful.
lines.cn: 也有证据表明，这种行为在社交上是有害的。

lines.t: It can leave people less satisfied with their face-to-face interactions, and it can generate feelings of resentment and jealousy.
lines.cn: 它会让人对面对面的交流更不满意，还可能引发怨恨和嫉妒的情绪。

lines.t: Now, the Journal of Applied Social Psychology has published a new study exploring the reasons for these effects.
lines.cn: 如今，《应用社会心理学杂志》发表了一项新研究，探讨这些影响的成因。

lines.t: The study included 128 mostly female student participants.
lines.cn: 该研究包括 128 名参与者，其中多为女性学生。

lines.t: The participants watched a three-minute animation in which two cartoon figures interacted and engaged in a conversation.
lines.cn: 参与者观看一段三分钟动画，其中两个卡通人物互动并交谈。

lines.t: The conversation couldn’t be heard, but could be detected through mouth movements.
lines.cn: 对话听不到声音，但可以通过嘴部动作看出在说话。

lines.t: Participants had to imagine themselves as the closest figure in the video, and then make judgments about the conversations and how they felt about their conversation partners.
lines.cn: 参与者需要把自己想象成视频中离镜头最近的那个人，然后对这段对话以及自己对交谈伙伴的感受做出判断。

lines.t: In one version of the experiment, the phone of the participant’s conversation partner remained unused on the table throughout the conversation.
lines.cn: 在实验的一个版本中，参与者交谈伙伴的手机始终放在桌上未被使用。

lines.t: In another version, their partner’s attention was quickly drawn to something on their phone, and they spent the rest of the time interacting with their phone.
lines.cn: 在另一个版本中，伙伴的注意力被手机上的某个东西迅速吸引，此后一直在玩手机。

lines.t: A third version involved the participant’s partner alternating between periods of interaction with their phone and periods where they ignored their phone.
lines.cn: 第三个版本中，参与者的伙伴在玩手机和放下手机之间交替。

lines.t: If you’ve experienced the similar situation, you probably won’t be surprised by the results of the experiments.
lines.cn: 如果你经历过类似情形，大概不会对实验结果感到意外。

lines.t: The participants had a negative view of phone use during social interactions.
lines.cn: 参与者对社交互动中使用手机持负面看法。

lines.t: The more it was present, the worse they considered both the quality of the interaction and the quality of the relationship.
lines.cn: 手机出现得越多，他们对互动质量和关系质量的评价就越差。

lines.t: The researchers believed that focusing on one’s phone instead of the person one is with has this effect because it’s seen as a form of social exclusion.
lines.cn: 研究者认为，只顾看手机而不顾眼前的人之所以产生这种影响，是因为它被视为一种社会排斥。

lines.t: They assert that the behavior is analogous to when people have no choice but to eat alone in the school cafeteria.
lines.cn: 他们断言，这种行为类似于人们不得不在学校食堂独自吃饭的情形。

lines.t: The twist is that this exclusion occurs while sharing a physical encounter and having a conversation.
lines.cn: 不同之处在于，这种排斥发生在共处同一空间、正在交谈的时候。

lines.t: Researchers found that the behavior had adverse effects on participants’ sense of belonging, need for meaning and self-esteem.
lines.cn: 研究者发现，这种行为对参与者的归属感、意义需求和自尊都产生了不良影响。

lines.t: These negative effects are similar to those caused by traditional forms of social exclusion.
lines.cn: 这些负面影响与传统的社交排斥形式所造成的影响相似。

lines.t: The new findings are important because they elaborate our understanding of a subtle but common aspect of our daily experience.
lines.cn: 这些新发现之所以重要，是因为它们加深了我们对日常经验中一个细微却普遍方面的理解。

lines.t: This common behavior can create vicious cycles of detachment even as we try to connect with others.
lines.cn: 这种常见行为会制造疏离的恶性循环——即便我们正试图与他人建立联系。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 7 组
tasks.context: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say travelers commonly complain about?

options.A: The ill treatment they get as tourists.
options.B: The nonprofessional business they see.
options.C: The impersonal accommodations.
options.D: The many adventures on their way.

questions.cn: 讲话者说旅行者通常抱怨什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们作为游客受到的恶劣对待。
optionsCn.B: 他们见到的非专业业务。
optionsCn.C: 千篇一律、缺乏人情味的住处。

questions.stem: What is said about bed-and-breakfast arrangements?

options.A: They have been the classic way to visit Europe.
options.B: They attract tourists with location and decoration.
options.C: They have long been competing with chain hotels.
options.D: They are in fact a completely new idea in America.

questions.cn: 关于“住宿加早餐”这种安排，文中说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们一直是游览欧洲的经典方式。
optionsCn.B: 它们以位置和装饰吸引游客。
optionsCn.C: 它们长期与连锁酒店竞争。
optionsCn.D: 它们在美国其实是全新的想法。

questions.stem: What is the first thing you have to consider if you want to start a B&B business?

options.B: Your family’s consent.
options.C: Your property.
options.D: Your personality.

questions.cn: 如果你想开办 B&B 生意，首先要考虑什么？

optionsCn.A: 你的财务状况。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say potential B&B hosts must be realistic about?

options.B: The number of guests to receive.
options.C: The facilities to provide.
options.D: Opportunities for income.

questions.cn: 讲话者说，有意经营 B&B 的房东必须对什么持现实态度？

optionsCn.A: 创业的成本。

lines.t: More and more people travel for a variety of reasons.
lines.cn: 越来越多的人出于各种原因出行。

lines.t: Many are tourists, but many venture for some personal or professional business.
lines.cn: 许多人是游客，但也有许多人为个人或职业事务而出行。

lines.t: Whatever the reason for traveling, a common complaint of travelers is the impersonal accommodations they find.
lines.cn: 无论出行的原因是什么，旅行者常见的一个抱怨是：住处千篇一律、没有人情味。

lines.t: After spending five consecutive nights in five similar hotels, the business traveler may find it difficult to remember what happened from day to day or even what towns were visited.
lines.cn: 连续五晚住五家相似的酒店后，商务旅客可能很难记清每天发生了什么，甚至去过哪些城镇。

lines.t: And the tourists may get the mistaken impression that all cities are pretty much the same, at least as far as decoration, food and service are concerned.
lines.cn: 而游客可能产生一种错觉：所有城市都大同小异，至少在装修、食物和服务方面如此。

lines.t: To combat this sense of impersonal sameness, travelers are taking advantage of in-home hospitality or bed-and-breakfast arrangements.
lines.cn: 为了对抗这种缺乏人情味的千篇一律，旅行者开始选择家庭寄宿或“住宿加早餐”的安排。

lines.t: B&Bs, I mean, bed-and-breakfast arrangements, are private homes which offer lodging and breakfast in a very personalized friendly setting.
lines.cn: B&B，也就是住宿加早餐，是指提供住宿和早餐的私人住宅，氛围非常个性化、友好。

lines.t: For decades, B&Bs have been the classic way to visit Europe, especially the British Isles.
lines.cn: 几十年来，B&B 一直是游览欧洲——尤其是不列颠群岛——的经典方式。

lines.t: And in fact, they are not really a new idea in America.
lines.cn: 事实上，它在美国也并不真正是新事物。

lines.t: The tradition dates back to colonial times when inns were few and far between, and the weary traveler had to depend on the kindness of strangers for a meal and a bed.
lines.cn: 这一传统可追溯到殖民时期，那时客栈稀少，疲惫的旅人只能依靠陌生人的善意获得一餐一宿。

lines.t: But the revival of B&Bs as desirable accommodations is a fairly recent phenomenon.
lines.cn: 但 B&B 作为理想住宿的复兴，是相当晚近的现象。

lines.t: If the idea of operating a B&B arouses your interest, there are several factors to consider before plunging into this business.
lines.cn: 如果经营 B&B 的想法引起了你的兴趣，在投身这一行之前有几个因素需要考虑。

lines.t: The first consideration is your property, not only the building itself, but the location.
lines.cn: 首先要考虑的是你的房产——不只是房子本身，还有位置。

lines.t: If you live near a famous historical site or in a popular destination such as New York City or Washington D.C., your home can be fairly simple yet still do well as a B&B.
lines.cn: 如果你住在著名历史遗址附近，或者纽约市、华盛顿特区这样热门的目的地，你的房子可以相当简朴，仍能作为 B&B 经营得不错。

lines.t: On the other hand, if your home is architecturally unique or has facilities for the traveler such as a private entrance, private bath or swimming pool, people may be willing to go some distance to reach you.
lines.cn: 反之，如果你的房子在建筑上独一无二，或者有私人入口、独立浴室、游泳池等便于旅客的设施，人们可能愿意走一段路来投宿。

lines.t: Another important factor is the lifestyle of you and your family.
lines.cn: 另一个重要因素是你和家人的生活方式。

lines.t: You must take into account whether all members of the family truly enjoy visitors, want to repeatedly discuss local sites and activities, and have the time and energy to handle the additional cooking, cleaning, laundry and the book keeping involved.
lines.cn: 你必须考虑：所有家庭成员是否真的喜欢来客、是否愿意一遍遍谈论当地景点和活动、是否有时间和精力应付额外的做饭、清洁、洗衣和记账工作。

lines.t: The final consideration is a financial one.
lines.cn: 最后要考虑的是财务问题。

lines.t: Potential B&B hosts must be realistic about opportunities for income.
lines.cn: 有意经营 B&B 的房东必须对收入机会持现实态度。

lines.t: While B&Bs usually have low initial costs, experts estimate it would take at least five rooms rented regularly for the host to earn a living from B&B.
lines.cn: 虽然 B&B 通常启动成本较低，但专家估计，房东至少要经常租出五间房，才能靠 B&B 谋生。
